review: Complete rival taxonomy and conditional grants retained. Horn necessary source and combination arguments inherit unresolved premise/attribute warrants; no new statistical independence penalty. Selected attributes description enumerates no fourth route.

cards.words: Horn argues that an ultimate necessary explanation cannot be limited or divided among competitors, while uniform natural order favors one universal source over plural or chaotic agency.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Horn directly engages Lataster’s rival taxonomy and offers identifiable narrowing reasons from ultimacy, absence of limitation, uniform natural order, and the distinction between a cause and what it causes. Principal limitation: Uniform laws weakly exclude coordinated plurality, the self-causing objection to pantheism assumes the disputed premise that the universe began, and deism receives only a compressed dismissal. Live burden: He must show why one unlimited source predicts the full body of debated evidence substantially better than coordinated deities, eternal pantheism, or deism under premises Lataster actually retains. Locked score: 76 The move is relevant, responsive, and a serious attempt to narrow generic supernaturalism, but its conditional assumptions and sparse comparative support do not establish that the named rival families have been excluded.

cards.words: Lataster conditionally grants supernaturalism and monotheism while distinguishing polytheistic, deistic, alternative-monotheistic, pantheistic, and mixed rivals through simplicity, hiddenness, suffering, and revelation comparisons among several competing supernatural explanations.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Lataster’s broad taxonomy demonstrates that generic supernaturalism does not entail classical theism and gives distinct comparative motivations for deistic, alternative-monotheistic, pantheistic, polytheistic, and mixed families. Principal limitation: Counting infinitely many descriptions does not determine probability, his principle-of-indifference measure is undefended, and repeated claims that rival families win exceed the priors and likelihoods actually supplied. Live burden: He need not prove any rival true to preserve the inferential gap, but affirmative claims of superior probability require principled family-level priors and evidence-sensitive likelihood comparisons. Locked score: 75 The move is centrally relevant, highly responsive, and substantively wide-ranging, yet unsupported probability foundations, dense proliferation of variants, and overstatement materially limit its coherence, warrant, clarity, and calibration.

cards.words: Horn combines necessity, personal design, and perfect goodness to argue that these distinct routes jointly converge on classical theism rather than merely supporting an unspecified supernatural cause.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Horn directly answers the generic-supernaturalism objection by explaining how contingency, design, and moral grounding are intended to contribute distinct attributes to one unlimited, personal, perfectly good foundation. Principal limitation: Each attribute inherits unresolved premises from its originating route, while the descriptive-versus-prescriptive distinction does not by itself establish that objective duties uniquely require a personal divine planner. Live burden: He must defend those individual bridges and show that the combined profile discriminates classical theism from the strongest rival concepts rather than merely collecting contested conclusions. Locked score: 78 The synthesis is relevant, understandable, and strongly responsive to the motion-level gap, but limited new warrant and Horn’s inaccurate claim that Lataster abandoned his objections constrain both cumulative force and calibration.

cards.words: Lataster defends deism, quasi-deism, and eternal pantheistic families by challenging required revelation, creation from nothing, substance dualism, and Horn’s brief dismissals of conditional rival possibilities.
cards.critique: Strongest feature: Lataster directly answers Horn’s deism and pantheism objections by identifying the added revelation claim and explaining why an eternal universe would avoid the alleged self-causation problem. Principal limitation: Compatibility with retained premises does not establish greater probability, and his assertions that pantheistic families win on both prior and likelihood grounds exceed the comparative analysis he provides. Live burden: He may keep representative rivals live by exposing Horn’s incomplete exclusions, but stronger claims of superiority require defensible priors and likelihoods rather than sheer descriptive multiplicity. Locked score: 81 The reply is highly responsive, source-specific, and important to the rival-concepts burden, while incomplete probability analysis and overstatement that theism cannot begin prevent unresolved alternatives from becoming a demonstrated rival victory.
